title: Tracked funding for malaria control in Uganda, US$ millions
what: Funding for malaria control as reported in the WHO World Malaria Report funding annex: national malaria programme (government, NMP line), Global Fund malaria disbursements, and the US President's Malaria Initiative (PMI). Excludes health-worker salaries and facility running costs paid by government, patient care, and household out-of-pocket spending.
caveats: The government (NMP) line is a narrow programme budget line; it fell from about 8.1 to 1.6 million between 2020 and 2021 because of how it was reported, not because of a verified cut. Do not read it as total government spending on malaria.
PMI figures are budgets as reported by the country, not disbursements.
Global Fund disbursements are lumpy from year to year, so comparisons use three-year averages.
UK bilateral funding (about 30 million in 2016, near zero after 2020) is left out of the totals, which makes the fall in money per case an understatement.

sources.funding: WHO World Malaria Report funding annexes, the latest edition covering each year (see edition): Global Fund = contributions reported by donors; PMI = contributions reported by countries; Government = national malaria programme (NMP) line
sources.globalFund: Same annexes, donor-reported Global Fund column (updated 29 Sept 2026; earlier values mixed older editions and Global Fund disbursement data)
sources.cases: WHO estimated malaria cases (Global Health Observatory, MALARIA_EST_CASES)
sources.cpi: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, CPI-U annual averages
